subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: 'Devore' (burnout) is a technique that...
options: Uses a chemical to dissolve fibres and leave a sheer pattern
questions.explain: Devore applies a chemical paste that burns away certain fibres, leaving a sheer patterned effect.

questions.q: A 'design brief' usually sets out...
options: The client's requirements and the target audience
questions.explain: A design brief defines the task, the client's needs and the intended target audience.

questions.q: Which is a synthetic (man-made) fibre?
questions.explain: Polyester is a synthetic fibre made from chemicals, unlike natural wool, silk and linen.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'annotation' in a sketchbook?
options: To explain your thinking, choices and development in words
To list the cost of materials
To fill empty space with decoration
questions.explain: Annotation uses written notes to explain your ideas, decisions and how your work is developing.

questions.q: In a composition, what is the 'focal point'?
options: The main area that draws the viewer's eye
The darkest area of the picture
questions.explain: The focal point is the part of the composition that attracts the viewer's attention first.

questions.q: Batik is a textile technique that uses what to resist dye?
questions.explain: In batik, hot wax is applied to fabric so the waxed areas resist the dye.

questions.q: Jackson Pollock is famous for which technique?
options: Dripping and pouring paint onto canvas
questions.explain: Jackson Pollock developed a 'drip' technique, pouring paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

questions.q: The RGB colour model is used mainly for...
questions.explain: RGB (red, green, blue) is the additive light model used by screens and digital devices.

questions.q: Throwing is a ceramics technique that uses...
options: A potter's wheel to shape clay
questions.explain: Throwing shapes clay into rounded forms by hand as it spins on a potter's wheel.

questions.q: Surrealism aimed to explore...
options: The dream world and the unconscious mind
questions.explain: Surrealism drew on dreams and the unconscious to create strange, irrational imagery.

questions.q: A 'photomontage' is created by...
options: Combining parts of several photographs into one image
questions.explain: A photomontage assembles fragments of several photographs into a single composite image.

questions.q: In weaving, the threads held under tension on the loom that run lengthways are the...
questions.explain: The warp threads run lengthways and are held taut on the loom while the weft is woven across them.

questions.q: Expressionism aims above all to convey...
options: The artist's inner emotion and feeling
questions.explain: Expressionism distorts colour and form to express the artist's emotional response rather than reality.

questions.q: Henri Cartier-Bresson is best known for the idea of the...
questions.explain: Cartier-Bresson coined the 'decisive moment', capturing a fleeting instant in street photography.

questions.q: Which formal element is described as a mark made by a moving point, having length and direction?
questions.explain: Line is the path of a moving point and is one of the most basic formal elements.

questions.q: 'Distressing' fabric in textiles means...
options: Deliberately fraying, tearing or wearing it for effect
questions.explain: Distressing intentionally frays, tears or ages fabric to create texture and a worn look.

questions.q: In a portrait, lighting placed to one side to create strong shadows and modelling is called...
questions.explain: Side lighting rakes across the face, producing shadows that reveal form and texture.

questions.q: Roy Lichtenstein's Pop Art is recognisable for its use of...
questions.explain: Lichtenstein imitated comic-book printing, using bold outlines and Ben-Day dots.

questions.q: Which assessment objective involves responding to the work of other artists?
options: Developing ideas through investigation of sources
questions.explain: Developing ideas requires investigating sources, including the work of relevant artists and cultures.

questions.q: Block printing on fabric works by...
options: Pressing an inked carved block onto the cloth
questions.explain: Block printing presses a raised, inked carved block onto fabric to repeat a motif.

questions.q: Bonding (interfacing) fabric with heat from an iron usually relies on...
options: A glue web or adhesive that melts
questions.explain: Bondaweb and fusible interfacing carry a heat-activated adhesive that melts to join fabrics.

questions.q: Frida Kahlo is best known for her...
questions.explain: Frida Kahlo is famous for intense, symbolic self-portraits drawing on her life and Mexican culture.
